at lokalisere.explanation: "At lokalisere" means "to locate", to find out where something is. It is used for a position that was unknown, such as a fault or a missing person: "Politiet lokaliserede bilen" (The police located the car).

sentence.da: Teknikeren kan **lokalisere** fejlen på få minutter.
sentence.en: The technician can locate the fault in a few minutes.

at lokke.explanation: "At lokke" means "to lure / tempt", to get someone to come or do something by offering something nice. With "med" (along) it means to coax someone to come along: "at lokke en med" (to lure someone along).

sentence.da: Duften af brød kan **lokke** folk ind i butikken.
sentence.en: The smell of bread can lure people into the store.

at love.explanation: "At love" means "to promise": "Jeg lover at komme" (I promise to come). To promise someone a gift: "Han lovede mig en gave" (He promised me a gift).

sentence.da: Kan du **love** mig, at du kommer i morgen?
sentence.en: Can you promise me that you will come tomorrow?

at lovgive.explanation: "At lovgive" means "to legislate": to make the official rules of a country. In Denmark this is the work of "Folketinget" (the Danish parliament). The word "lovgivning" (legislation) is much more common than "at lovgive": "dansk lovgivning" (Danish legislation).

sentence.da: Politikerne kan **lovgive** om, hvem der må køre bil.
sentence.en: The politicians can legislate about who may drive a car.

at lufte hunden.explanation: "At lufte hunden" means "to walk the dog". It comes from "lufte" (to air out), so the idea is giving the dog fresh air.

sentence.da: Hver morgen skal jeg **lufte hunden** i parken.
sentence.en: Every morning I have to walk the dog in the park.

at lufte ud.explanation: "At lufte ud" means "to air out", to let fresh air into a room. "Ud" means "out": the stale air goes out, as in "at gå ud" (to go out) and "at hælde ud" (to pour out).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lufte ud**, fordi der lugter dårligt her.
sentence.en: I want to air out because it smells bad in here.

at luge.explanation: "At luge" means "to weed": to pull out the plants you do not want from the soil in a garden. What you pull is called "ukrudt" (weeds): "luge ukrudt" (to pull weeds).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **luge** bedet, så blomsterne kan vokse.
sentence.en: I will weed the bed so the flowers can grow.

at lugte.explanation: "At lugte" means "to smell", both to give off a smell and to notice a smell. To describe the smell, add "godt" (good) or "dårligt" (bad): "Det lugter godt" (It smells good).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **lugte** kaffe fra køkkenet.
sentence.en: I can smell coffee from the kitchen.

at lukke.explanation: "At lukke" means "to close", for things such as a door, a window, a shop or a bag. To say when a shop shuts: "Vi lukker om ti minutter" (We close in ten minutes).

sentence.da: Kan du **lukke** vinduet? Det er koldt.
sentence.en: Can you close the window? It is cold.

at lyde.explanation: "At lyde" means "to sound", how something seems to you when you hear about it: "Det lyder godt" (That sounds good). To say you hear a sound, use "at høre" (to hear): "Jeg hører musik" (I hear music).

sentence.da: Det kan **lyde** som en god idé.
sentence.en: It may sound like a good idea.

at lykkes.explanation: "At lykkes" means "to succeed" or "to work out". Start with "det" (it), then add the person who succeeds: "mig" (me), "dig" (you), "ham" (him). "Det lykkedes mig at finde den" (I succeeded in finding it).

sentence.da: Jeg håber, det vil **lykkes** mig at finde et job.
sentence.en: I hope I will succeed in finding a job.

at lyne.explanation: "At lyne" means "to flash with lightning" and always goes with "det", like "it" in English weather talk: "Det lyner og tordner" (There is lightning and thunder).

sentence.da: Himlen er mørk, og det vil snart **lyne**.
sentence.en: The sky is dark, and there will soon be lightning.

at lyne op.explanation: "At lyne op" means "to unzip", to open a coat or a pair of trousers by pulling the slider down. "Op" (up) works the same way in "at knappe op" (to unbutton): both open something that was closed.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **lyne op**, når lynlåsen sidder fast.
sentence.en: I cannot unzip when the zipper is stuck.

at lyse.explanation: "At lyse" means "to shine" or "to give light": "Månen lyser" (The moon is shining). You can aim light at something with "på" (on): "Jeg lyste på døren med lommelygten" (I shone the flashlight on the door).

sentence.da: Lampen skal **lyse** i mørket.
sentence.en: The lamp has to shine in the dark.

at lyse op.explanation: "At lyse op" means "to light up": "Hendes ansigt lyste op" (Her face lit up). It also works for a lamp in a room: "Lampen lyser rummet op" (The lamp lights up the room).

sentence.da: Hendes ansigt vil **lyse op**, når hun ser dig.
sentence.en: Her face will light up when she sees you.

at lytte.explanation: "At lytte" means "to listen" on purpose: "Jeg lyttede til musikken" (I listened to the music). "At høre" (to hear) means just noticing a sound, wanted or not: "Jeg hørte en lyd" (I heard a sound).

sentence.da: Du skal **lytte**, når læreren taler.
sentence.en: You have to listen when the teacher talks.

at lytte til.explanation: "At lytte til" means "to listen to": "Jeg lytter til radioen" (I listen to the radio). "At høre" (to hear) only means noticing a sound: "Jeg hørte dig ikke" (I did not hear you).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **lytte til** musik i aften.
sentence.en: I want to listen to music tonight.

at lyve.explanation: "At lyve" means "to lie", as in telling a lie: "Du lyver!" (You are lying!) Lying down uses a different word, "at ligge" (to lie down): "Jeg ligger i sengen" (I am lying in bed).

sentence.da: Du må ikke **lyve** for mig.
sentence.en: You must not lie to me.

at låne.explanation: "At låne" means "to borrow" and also "to lend". You can tell which meaning is intended from the context of the sentence. "Kan jeg låne din pen?" means "Can I borrow your pen?". "Jeg låner dig min cykel" means "I lend you my bike". To make the meaning clear, Danes sometimes say "låne af" (borrow from) and "låne ud" (lend out).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **låne** en bog på biblioteket.
sentence.en: I want to borrow a book at the library.

at låse.explanation: "At låse" means "to lock": "Han låser cyklen" (He locks the bike). Adding "op" (up) gives the opposite: "at låse op" (to unlock).

sentence.da: Husk at **låse** døren, når du går.
sentence.en: Remember to lock the door when you leave.

at låse op.explanation: "At låse op" means "to unlock". The word "op" (up) comes last: "Hun låser skabet op" (She unlocks the cabinet).

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke **låse op**, fordi jeg har glemt nøglen.
sentence.en: I cannot unlock because I have forgotten the key.

at lægge.explanation: "At lægge" means "to lay down": to put something down flat, as in "Jeg lægger barnet i sengen" (I put the baby in bed). Do not mix it up with "at ligge" (to be lying somewhere): "Bogen ligger på bordet" (The book is lying on the table).

sentence.da: Du skal **lægge** tøjet i skabet.
sentence.en: You have to put the clothes in the closet.

at lægge fra sig.explanation: "At lægge fra sig" means "to put down" what you are holding: "Han lagde bogen fra sig" (He put the book down).

sentence.da: Hun skal **lægge fra sig** det, hun har i hænderne.
sentence.en: She has to put down what she has in her hands.

at lægge mærke til.explanation: "At lægge mærke til" means "to notice": "Jeg lagde mærke til hans nye jakke" (I noticed his new jacket).

sentence.da: Hun vil nok **lægge mærke til** din nye frisure.
sentence.en: She will probably notice your new haircut.

at lægge planer.explanation: "At lægge planer" means "to make plans", often for a trip or an event. "Lægge" means "to put", so it is literally "to lay plans", as in English.

sentence.da: Vi vil **lægge planer** for sommeren.
sentence.en: We want to make plans for the summer.

at lægge på.explanation: "At lægge på" means "to hang up", to end a phone call: "Hun lagde på uden at sige farvel" (She hung up without saying goodbye).

sentence.da: Jeg må **lægge på**, fordi bussen kommer.
sentence.en: I have to hang up because the bus is coming.

at lægge sammen.explanation: "At lægge sammen" means "to add up": "Jeg lægger to og tre sammen" (I add two and three together).

sentence.da: Jeg kan **lægge sammen** i hovedet.
sentence.en: I can add up in my head.

at lægge sig.explanation: "At lægge sig" means "to lie down": "Jeg lægger mig på sofaen" (I lie down on the sofa). To say you are already lying there, use "at ligge" (to lie): "Jeg ligger i sengen" (I am lying in bed).

sentence.da: Han er træt og vil **lægge sig** på sofaen.
sentence.en: He is tired and wants to lie down on the sofa.

at lægge vægt på.explanation: "At lægge vægt på" means "to emphasize", to say that something is especially important. Literally it is "to put weight on" something: "Vi lægger vægt på kvalitet" (We emphasize quality).

sentence.da: Skolen vil **lægge vægt på**, at børnene får frisk luft.
sentence.en: The school wants to emphasize that the children get fresh air.

at lække.explanation: "At lække" means "to leak", when liquid or gas gets out through a hole. It can also be used for secret information: "Nogen lækkede dokumentet" (Someone leaked the document).

sentence.da: Taget begynder at **lække**, når det regner meget.
sentence.en: The roof starts to leak when it rains a lot.

at læne sig.explanation: "At læne sig" means "to lean", to rest your body at a slant against something. It always has "sig" (oneself), which becomes "mig" (myself), "dig" (yourself) and so on: "Jeg læner mig mod væggen" (I lean against the wall).

sentence.da: Han vil **læne sig** tilbage og slappe af.
sentence.en: He wants to lean back and relax.

at lære.explanation: "At lære" means "to learn" and also "to teach": "Jeg lærer dansk" (I learn Danish) and "Hun lærer mig dansk" (She teaches me Danish). You can tell which meaning is intended from the context of the sentence. "En lærer" (a teacher) is spelled the same as "lærer" in "Hun lærer mig dansk". Do not mix "at lære" up with "at læse" (to read): "Jeg læser en bog" (I am reading a book).

sentence.da: Børn kan **lære** meget i skolen.
sentence.en: Children can learn a lot at school.

at lære at kende.explanation: "At lære at kende" means "to get to know" a person: "Jeg lærer ham at kende" (I am getting to know him).

forms.da: jeg har lært ham at kende
forms.en: I have gotten to know him

sentence.da: Det er dejligt at **lære at kende** nye mennesker.
sentence.en: It is nice to get to know new people.

at lære udenad.explanation: "At lære udenad" means "to memorize", to learn something by heart so you can say it without looking: "Jeg lærer ordene udenad" (I memorize the words). "At lære" (to learn) alone does not mean by heart.

sentence.da: Eleverne skal **lære udenad** til prøven i morgen.
sentence.en: The students have to memorize for the test tomorrow.

at læse.explanation: "At læse" means "to read": "Jeg læser en bog" (I am reading a book). It also means to study a subject at university: "Hun læser medicin" (She studies medicine). Do not mix it up with "at lære" (to learn): "Jeg lærer dansk" (I am learning Danish).

sentence.da: Min datter kan **læse** og skrive.
sentence.en: My daughter can read and write.

at læse om.explanation: "At læse om" means "to read about" a topic: "Jeg læser om dansk historie" (I am reading about Danish history). To read a book itself, use "at læse" (to read) with no "om": "Jeg læser en bog" (I am reading a book).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne **læse om** Island.
sentence.en: I would like to read about Iceland.

at læse op.explanation: "At læse op" means "to read aloud" to other people: "Læreren læser op for klassen" (The teacher reads aloud to the class). It also means to read out a list: "Han læste navnene op" (He read out the names).

sentence.da: Kan du **læse op** for os?
sentence.en: Can you read aloud to us?

at læse til.explanation: "At læse til" means "to study to become": "Han læser til læge" (He is studying to become a doctor). Without "til", "at læse" (to read) can also mean "to study" a subject.

sentence.da: Min søster vil **læse til** læge i København.
sentence.en: My sister wants to study to become a doctor in Copenhagen.

at løbe.explanation: "At løbe" means "to run", for sport or in a hurry: "Jeg løber hver morgen" (I run every morning). It is also used for anything that flows, such as a nose: "Min næse løber" (My nose is running). For running out of something, use "at løbe tør for" (to run out of).

sentence.da: Jeg vil **løbe** hurtigt for at nå bussen.
sentence.en: I want to run fast to catch the bus.

at løbe efter.explanation: "At løbe efter" means "to run after": "Hunden løber efter bolden" (The dog runs after the ball). For a real chase, use "at jage" (to chase): "Katten jager musen" (The cat chases the mouse).

sentence.da: Jeg måtte **løbe efter** bussen i morges.
sentence.en: I had to run after the bus this morning.

at løbe en tur.explanation: "At løbe en tur" means "to go for a run": "Jeg løber en tur efter arbejde" (I go for a run after work). The same pattern works for other activities: "at gå en tur" (to go for a walk).

forms.en: I have gone for a run

related.en: to go for a bike ride

sentence.da: Når solen skinner, vil jeg **løbe en tur**.
sentence.en: When the sun shines, I want to go for a run.

at løbe ind i.explanation: "At løbe ind i" means "to run into". You use it when you bump into something by accident: "Jeg løb ind i en dør" (I ran into a door). You also use it when you meet someone by chance: "Jeg løb ind i min nabo" (I ran into my neighbor).

sentence.da: I byen kan jeg **løbe ind i** en gammel ven.
sentence.en: In town I might run into an old friend.

at løbe på skøjter.explanation: "At løbe på skøjter" means "to ice-skate". Danish literally says "run on skates", built from løbe (run) and på skøjter (on skates).

sentence.da: Om vinteren kan vi **løbe på skøjter** på isen.
sentence.en: In winter we can ice-skate on the ice.

at løbe tør for.explanation: "At løbe tør for" means "to run out of", when you have none left: "Vi løb tør for mælk" (We ran out of milk).

sentence.da: Bilen kan **løbe tør for** benzin på vejen.
sentence.en: The car can run out of gas on the road.

at løbe væk.explanation: "At løbe væk" means "to run away", to leave by running, often from danger or from home: "Drengen løb væk fra hunden" (The boy ran away from the dog).

sentence.da: Barnet må ikke **løbe væk** fra os.
sentence.en: The child must not run away from us.

at løfte.explanation: "At løfte" means "to lift" and "to raise": "Jeg løfter barnet" (I lift the child) and "Hun løfter armen" (She raises her arm). Do not mix it up with "et løfte" (a promise): "Jeg giver dig et løfte" (I give you a promise).

sentence.da: Han kan **løfte** tunge ting alene.
sentence.en: He can lift heavy things alone.

at løse.explanation: "At løse" means "to solve": "Jeg løser opgaven" (I solve the task). It also means "to untie": "Hun løste knuden" (She untied the knot).

sentence.da: Vi kan **løse** problemet sammen.
sentence.en: We can solve the problem together.

at løslade.explanation: "At løslade" means "to release" a person from prison or police custody. You mostly see it as "blive løsladt" (to be released): "Han blev løsladt i går" (He was released yesterday).

sentence.da: Efter to år i fængsel vil de **løslade** ham.
sentence.en: After two years in prison, they will release him.

en ladcykel.explanation: "En ladcykel" means "a cargo bike", a bike with a big box on the front for kids or shopping. The first part, "lad", is the open load area.

sentence.da: Der er plads til mange indkøb i min **ladcykel**.
sentence.en: There is room for a lot of groceries in my cargo bike.

en lade.explanation: "En lade" means "a barn", where a farmer keeps hay and machines. Do not mix it up with "at lade" (to let), which is spelled the same: "Jeg lader dig gå" (I let you go).

sentence.da: Bonden har hø og maskiner i sin **lade**.
sentence.en: The farmer keeps hay and machines in his barn.

en ladestander.explanation: "En ladestander" means "a charging station", the post where you connect a car to charge it. It is built from lade (charge) and stander (post). The word "at lade" (to charge) also works for a phone: "Jeg lader min telefon" (I am charging my phone).

sentence.da: Jeg parkerer ved en **ladestander** og lader min bil.
sentence.en: I park at a charging station and charge my car.

en lagerarbejder.explanation: "En lagerarbejder" means "a warehouse worker", someone who receives, stores and packs items in a "lager" (a warehouse or stock room).

sentence.da: Som **lagerarbejder** pakker han varer og kører dem ud med en truck.
sentence.en: As a warehouse worker he packs goods and drives them out with a forklift.

en lagkage.explanation: "En lagkage" means "a layer cake". It is built from et lag (a layer) and en kage (a cake), with cream or jam between the layers of sponge cake.

sentence.da: Vi spiser **lagkage** med fløde til fødselsdagen.
sentence.en: We eat layer cake with cream for the birthday.

en lampe.explanation: "En lampe" means "a lamp", a light that stands on a table or the floor, or hangs on a wall.

sentence.da: Jeg tænder en **lampe** i det mørke rum.
sentence.en: I turn on a lamp in the dark room.

en lampeskærm.explanation: "En lampeskærm" means "a lampshade", the cover that softens the glow of a lamp. It is built from lampe (lamp) and skærm (shade). "Skærm" also means a screen: "en computerskærm" (a computer screen).

sentence.da: Pæren er skjult bag en gul **lampeskærm**.
sentence.en: The bulb is hidden behind a yellow lampshade.

en landevej.explanation: "En landevej" means "a country road", a road between towns outside the big cities. It is slower than a highway: "Vi kører ad landevejen i stedet for motorvejen" (We take the country road instead of the highway).

sentence.da: Vi kører langsomt på en smal **landevej**.
sentence.en: We drive slowly on a narrow country road.

en landing.explanation: "En landing" means "a landing", mostly for a plane touching down. It comes from "at lande" (to land).

sentence.da: Flyet havde en rolig **landing** i Kastrup.
sentence.en: The plane had a smooth landing in Kastrup.

en landingsbane.explanation: "En landingsbane" means "a runway", the long paved strip that planes land on. It is built from landing (landing) and bane (track). "Bane" also means a court: "en tennisbane" (a tennis court).

sentence.da: Flyet lander på en lang **landingsbane**.
sentence.en: The plane lands on a long runway.

en landmand.explanation: "En landmand" means "a farmer", built from land (countryside) and mand (man). Danish leaves out "en" (a) when naming a job: "Han er landmand" (He is a farmer).

sentence.da: En **landmand** har køer og arbejder på marken.
sentence.en: A farmer has cows and works in the field.

en landsby.explanation: "En landsby" means "a village", a small place in the countryside, with some houses and often a church.

sentence.da: Der bor kun hundrede mennesker i vores **landsby**.
sentence.en: Only a hundred people live in our village.

en landskamp.explanation: "En landskamp" means "an international match", a sports match where teams from two countries play each other, such as in soccer or handball.

sentence.da: Danmark spiller **landskamp** mod Sverige i aften.
sentence.en: Denmark plays an international match against Sweden tonight.

en larve.explanation: "En larve" means "a caterpillar" or "a larva", the young stage of an insect, which eats and grows before changing into the adult form.

sentence.da: En **larve** bliver til en sommerfugl, når den er færdig med at vokse.
sentence.en: A caterpillar turns into a butterfly when it has finished growing.

en laser.explanation: "En laser" means "a laser", a very narrow, strong beam of light used for measuring, cutting and medical treatment.

sentence.da: Lægen bruger en **laser** til at operere øjnene.
sentence.en: The doctor uses a laser to operate on the eyes.

en last.explanation: "En last" means "a cargo", the goods a ship carries, and also "a vice", a bad habit. The opposite of a vice is "en dyd" (a virtue).

sentence.da: Skibet sejler med en tung **last** af korn.
sentence.en: The ship sails with a heavy cargo of grain.

en lastbil.explanation: "En lastbil" means "a truck", a large vehicle for carrying goods. It is built from last (load) and bil (car). "Bil" ends many vehicle words, such as "en brandbil" (a fire engine).

sentence.da: En **lastbil** kører med varer til butikkerne.
sentence.en: A truck carries goods to the stores.

en lastbilchauffør.explanation: "En lastbilchauffør" means "a truck driver". It is built from en lastbil (a truck) and en chauffør (a driver). The "ch" is said like "sh", as in French, so "chauffør" sounds like "sjofør".

sentence.da: Min far er **lastbilchauffør** og kører meget.
sentence.en: My father is a truck driver and drives a lot.

en latter.explanation: "En latter" means "laughter", the sound people make when something is funny. It is mostly used without "en": "Der var meget latter" (There was a lot of laughter).

sentence.da: Fra legepladsen kunne vi høre børnenes **latter**.
sentence.en: From the playground we could hear the children's laughter.

en ledelse.explanation: "En ledelse" means "management" or "leadership", the people who run a company and the act of leading.

sentence.da: Firmaets **ledelse** bestemmer, hvordan pengene skal bruges.
sentence.en: The company's management decides how the money is to be used.

en leder.explanation: "En leder" means "a leader" or "a manager", someone who guides a team. For the top person of a whole company, use "en direktør" (a director).

sentence.da: Vores **leder** fordeler arbejdet mellem os.
sentence.en: Our manager divides the work among us.

en ledning.explanation: "En ledning" means "a cord" or "a cable" that carries electricity, such as the one on a lamp.

sentence.da: Telefonen får strøm gennem en **ledning**.
sentence.en: The phone gets power through a cord.

en ledsager.explanation: "En ledsager" means "a companion", a person who goes along with someone else, to keep them company or to help. On an invitation, it is the person you may bring with you.

sentence.da: Du må gerne tage en **ledsager** med til festen.
sentence.en: You are welcome to bring a companion to the party.

en leg.explanation: "En leg" means "a game" in the sense of play, mostly for children. For a board game or sports game, use "et spil" (a game).

sentence.da: Børnene har fundet på en ny **leg**.
sentence.en: The children have invented a new game.

en legende.explanation: "En legende" means "a legend", an old story handed down over generations, and also a famous person who is a legend in their field: "Han er en legende i dansk fodbold" (He is a legend in Danish football). Do not mix it up with "legende børn" (playing children), which comes from "at lege" (to play).

sentence.da: Der findes en gammel **legende** om en drage i søen.
sentence.en: There is an old legend about a dragon in the lake.

en legeplads.explanation: "En legeplads" means "a playground", a place with swings and slides for children.

sentence.da: Børnene løber rundt og leger på en **legeplads**.
sentence.en: The children run around and play on a playground.

en legetøjsbutik.explanation: "En legetøjsbutik" means "a toy store", a shop that sells legetøj (toys) for children, such as dolls and games.

sentence.da: Børnene elsker at kigge på dukker i en **legetøjsbutik**.
sentence.en: The children love looking at dolls in a toy store.

en lejebolig.explanation: "En lejebolig" means "a rental home", an apartment or house that you live in but do not own.

sentence.da: Vi bor i en **lejebolig**, så vi betaler husleje hver måned.
sentence.en: We live in a rental home, so we pay rent every month.

en lejekontrakt.explanation: "En lejekontrakt" means "a lease", the written agreement for a home you pay to live in. It is built from at leje (to rent) and en kontrakt (a contract). "Kontrakt" also appears in "en arbejdskontrakt" (a work contract).

sentence.da: Din husleje står i en **lejekontrakt**.
sentence.en: Your rent is written in a lease.

en lejer.explanation: "En lejer" means "a tenant", the person who rents a home from the owner. The other side is "en udlejer" (a landlord), who owns the home and rents it out.

sentence.da: Jeg er **lejer** og ejer ikke lejligheden.
sentence.en: I am a tenant and do not own the apartment.

en lejlighed.explanation: "En lejlighed" means "an apartment", a home that is one of several in a building.

sentence.da: Vi bor på anden sal i en **lejlighed**.
sentence.en: We live on the second floor in an apartment.

en lejr.explanation: "En lejr" means "a camp", a place where people stay for a while: "Klassen tager på lejr" (The class goes to camp). To set up a camp, say "at slå lejr" (to pitch camp).

sentence.da: Børnene sover i telte i vores **lejr**.
sentence.en: The kids sleep in tents in our camp.

en lejrskole.explanation: "En lejrskole" means "a school camp trip", a trip of several days when pupils travel together with their teachers and sleep away from home. You say "tage på lejrskole" (go on a school camp trip), without "en".

sentence.da: Vores klasse skal på **lejrskole** til Bornholm i næste uge.
sentence.en: Our class is going on a school camp trip to Bornholm next week.

en lektion.explanation: "En lektion" means "a lesson", one class period at school: "Vi har en lektion i engelsk" (We have a lesson in English). Do not mix it up with "lektier" (homework): "Jeg laver lektier" (I do homework).

sentence.da: Den næste **lektion** begynder om fem minutter.
sentence.en: The next lesson begins in five minutes.

en leopard.explanation: "En leopard" means "a leopard", a big spotted wild cat. It looks like "en gepard" (a cheetah), but a leopard is heavier and often climbs trees.

sentence.da: En **leopard** klatrer op i træet og sover.
sentence.en: A leopard climbs up the tree and sleeps.

en letbane.explanation: "En letbane" means "a light rail", an electric train that looks like a tram. It runs on streets in town and faster out in the country.

sentence.da: Der kører en **letbane** gennem Aarhus.
sentence.en: A light rail runs through Aarhus.

en lever.explanation: "En lever" means "a liver", the large organ on the right side of your body. Animal livers are eaten too. Do not mix it up with "at leve" (to live): "Jeg lever" (I live).

sentence.da: Din **lever** renser blodet og hjælper kroppen med at fordøje maden.
sentence.en: Your liver cleans the blood and helps the body digest food.

en leverandør.explanation: "En leverandør" means "a supplier", a company or person that regularly provides goods or services to a business. The business that buys from it is "en kunde" (a customer).

sentence.da: Vores **leverandør** sender friske grøntsager til restauranten hver morgen.
sentence.en: Our supplier sends fresh vegetables to the restaurant every morning.

en levering.explanation: "En levering" means "a delivery", goods brought to your home by a store or a courier, often after an online order.

sentence.da: Vi venter på en **levering** fra butikken.
sentence.en: We are waiting for a delivery from the store.

en leveringstid.explanation: "En leveringstid" means "a delivery time", the number of days between ordering something and receiving it. Do not mix it up with "en leveringsdato" (a delivery date), which is one fixed day.

sentence.da: En lang **leveringstid** betyder, at pakken kommer sent.
sentence.en: A long delivery time means the package arrives late.

en lidelse.explanation: "En lidelse" means "a disorder" or "suffering". As a health word, it is a long-lasting problem with the body or mind, such as asthma. In writing, it can also mean suffering in general: "Der var megen lidelse i krigen" (There was much suffering in the war).

sentence.da: Astma er en kronisk **lidelse** i lungerne.
sentence.en: Asthma is a chronic disorder of the lungs.

en lift.explanation: "En lift" means "a ride in someone's car", for example when a friend takes you home. Ask for one with "Kan jeg få en lift?" (Can I get a ride?). You do not use it for paid transport like a taxi.

forms.en: I will give you a ride

sentence.da: Min nabo gav mig en **lift** i sin bil.
sentence.en: My neighbor gave me a ride in his car.

en liga.explanation: "En liga" means "a league", a group of teams that play against each other through a season. The top Danish soccer league is called "Superligaen" (the Super League).

sentence.da: Alle holdene i en **liga** spiller mod hinanden hele sæsonen.
sentence.en: All the teams in a league play against each other all season.

en ligevægt.explanation: "En ligevægt" means "an equilibrium", a state where forces or amounts are equal, so nothing tips to one side. It is also a person's sense of balance: "miste ligevægten" (to lose your balance).

sentence.da: Priserne finder en **ligevægt**, når udbud og efterspørgsel er lige store.
sentence.en: Prices find an equilibrium when supply and demand are equal.

en lighed.explanation: "En lighed" means "a similarity", something two things have in common. It is often paired with its opposite: "ligheder og forskelle" (similarities and differences).

sentence.da: Der er stor **lighed** mellem de to brødre.
sentence.en: There is a strong similarity between the two brothers.

en lighter.explanation: "En lighter" means "a lighter", the small tool you click to make a flame.

sentence.da: Jeg kan ikke tænde bålet uden min **lighter**.
sentence.en: I can't light the fire without my lighter.

en ligning.explanation: "En ligning" means "an equation", a statement in math where two sides are equal and you find the unknown number, often called x.

sentence.da: I en **ligning** er der altid et lighedstegn.
sentence.en: In an equation there is always an equals sign.

en lillebror.explanation: "En lillebror" means "a little brother", a brother who is younger than you. It is built from lille (little) and en bror (a brother). He stays your "lillebror" when he is grown up: "Min lillebror er 40 år" (My little brother is 40 years old).

sentence.da: Min **lillebror** er fem år.
sentence.en: My little brother is five years old.

en lillesøster.explanation: "En lillesøster" means "a little sister", a sister who is younger than you. It is built from lille (little) and en søster (a sister). She stays your "lillesøster" when she is grown up: "Min lillesøster er 40 år" (My little sister is 40 years old).

sentence.da: Min **lillesøster** er tre år.
sentence.en: My little sister is three years old.

en lime.explanation: "En lime" means "a lime", a small, sour, green citrus fruit.

sentence.da: Jeg presser en **lime** over fisken.
sentence.en: I squeeze a lime over the fish.

en lineal.explanation: "En lineal" means "a ruler", the tool for measuring and drawing straight lines. A ruler of a country is "en hersker" (a sovereign).

sentence.da: Jeg måler papiret med en **lineal**.
sentence.en: I measure the paper with a ruler.

en linje.explanation: "En linje" means "a line". It is also a bus or train line: "Tag linje 5" (Take line 5). For people waiting in a line, say "en kø" (a queue).

sentence.da: Tegn en lige **linje** på papiret.
sentence.en: Draw a straight line on the paper.
